name: Congenital Renal Artery Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Renal Artery Stenosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstration of renal artery narrowing on angiography or Doppler ultrasound
Early onset hypertension, especially refractory or severe
Exclusion of acquired causes of renal artery stenosis such as atherosclerosis or fibromuscular dysplasia
Evidence of impaired renal function or asymmetry in kidney size

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of imaging-confirmed renal artery stenosis with early onset hypertension and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical presentation; genetic testing is not routinely available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe refractory hypertension in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: very high blood pressure in young children
early childhood difficult to control high blood pressure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Asymmetric renal size detected on imaging
searchTerms: one kidney larger than the other
kidneys of different sizes seen on imaging

common.symptomName: Abdominal bruit over affected renal artery
searchTerms: whooshing sound in belly near kidney
increased hormone causing blood pressure rise

common.symptomName: Reduced glomerular filtration rate in affected kidney

searchTerms: failure to gain weight as expected

occasional.symptomName: Polyuria due to impaired renal function
searchTerms: increased urine output due to kidney issues
polyuria caused by impaired renal function

occasional.symptomName: Left ventricular hypertrophy secondary to hypertension
searchTerms: thickened heart muscle from high blood pressure
left ventricular thickening due to hypertension

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary edema secondary to severe hypertension
searchTerms: fluid in lungs from high blood pressure
lung swelling due to severe hypertension

laboratory: Impaired renal function tests (elevated serum creatinine)
imaging: Renal artery stenosis demonstrated by Doppler ultrasound
Angiographic evidence of renal artery narrowing
Asymmetric kidney size on ultrasound or CT
genetic: No specific genetic markers identified; diagnosis is clinical and radiological
other: Hypertension refractory to standard antihypertensive therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Typically affects young to middle-aged females
Characteristic 'string of beads' appearance on angiography
Occurs mainly in older adults with cardiovascular risk factors

redFlags: Severe hypertension refractory to multiple antihypertensive agents
Signs of hypertensive emergency such as encephalopathy or pulmonary edema
references: Kaplan BS, et al. Pediatric Renovascular Hypertension. Pediatr Nephrol. 2019.
Orphanet: Congenital renal artery stenosis. ORPHA:97598.
